title: Proverbs Chapter 23 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 23 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 23 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 23.

questions.question: When sitting to eat with a ruler, what should you do according to Proverbs 23:1?
options: Consider diligently what is before thee
Ignore the food and focus on conversation
questions.correctAnswer: Consider diligently what is before thee
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:1 instructs to consider diligently what is before thee when sitting to eat with a ruler.

questions.question: What extreme metaphor is used in Proverbs 23:2 to warn against being given to appetite?
options: Put a knife to thy throat
questions.correctAnswer: Put a knife to thy throat
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:2 uses the metaphor 'put a knife to thy throat' to warn a man given to appetite.

questions.question: Why should one not desire the dainties of a ruler according to Proverbs 23:3?
options: They are meant only for the ruler
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:3 states that the dainties of a ruler are deceitful meat, hence one should not desire them.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:4 advise about laboring to be rich?
options: Labour not to be rich; cease from thine own wisdom
Work harder to increase your wealth
questions.correctAnswer: Labour not to be rich; cease from thine own wisdom
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:4 advises to labor not to be rich and to cease from one's own wisdom.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:5, what happens to riches?
options: They fly away as an eagle toward heaven
questions.correctAnswer: They fly away as an eagle toward heaven
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:5 says riches certainly make themselves wings and fly away as an eagle toward heaven.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:6 warn about eating the bread of someone with an evil eye?
options: Do not eat it nor desire his dainty meats
It is a sign of friendship
questions.correctAnswer: Do not eat it nor desire his dainty meats
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:6 warns not to eat the bread of him that hath an evil eye, nor desire his dainty meats.

questions.question: What does a person with an evil eye say when inviting you to eat and drink, according to Proverbs 23:7?
options: Eat and drink, but his heart is not with thee
Eat and drink with joy and love
questions.correctAnswer: Eat and drink, but his heart is not with thee
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:7 explains that such a person says 'Eat and drink' to thee, but his heart is not with thee.

questions.question: What will happen to the morsel you have eaten from the person with an evil eye, according to Proverbs 23:8?
options: Thou shalt vomit it up and lose thy sweet words
Thou shalt be blessed with abundance
Thou shalt share it with friends
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt vomit it up and lose thy sweet words
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:8 states that the morsel eaten from such a person shalt thou vomit up and lose thy sweet words.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 23:9 instructs us to speak in the ears of a fool to teach him wisdom.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:9 says, 'Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.'

questions.question: What should not be removed according to Proverbs 23:10?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:10 commands not to remove the old landmark.

questions.question: Who is the mighty redeemer that will plead the cause of the fatherless according to Proverbs 23:11?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:11 states that their redeemer is mighty and shall plead their cause.

questions.question: What should one apply their heart unto, according to Proverbs 23:12?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:12 says to apply thine heart unto instruction and thine ears to the words of knowledge.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 23:4 encourages us to labor to be rich by our own wisdom.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:4 advises to labor not to be rich and to cease from thine own wisdom.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 23:1 advises careful consideration when eating with a ruler.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:1 says, 'When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee.'

questions.question: In Proverbs 23, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Consider what is before thee when eating with a ruler
questions.correctAnswer: Consider what is before thee when eating with a ruler
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:1 is the first instruction given in the chapter, before other instructions such as laboring not to be rich (v4), removing landmarks (v10), or applying heart to instruction (v12).

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 23 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 23 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:13, what is the outcome if a child is disciplined with the rod?
options: The child will resent the discipline
The child will be punished severely
The child will forget the lesson
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:13 explicitly states 'Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.' This verse teaches that discipline, when applied properly, does not cause death but is a form of correction.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 23:14 describe the purpose of physical correction for a child?
options: To deliver his soul from hell
questions.correctAnswer: To deliver his soul from hell
questions.explanation: Verse 14 says, 'Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell,' indicating that correction serves a spiritual purpose, saving the child from eternal harm.

questions.question: What emotional response does the wise heart of a son bring to the father's heart according to Proverbs 23:15?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:15 states, 'My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine,' showing the joy a father feels when his child has wisdom.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:16, what causes the speaker’s 'reins' to rejoice?
options: When thy lips speak right things
questions.correctAnswer: When thy lips speak right things
questions.explanation: Verse 16 says, 'Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things,' indicating that proper speech brings deep joy.

questions.question: What advice does Proverbs 23:17 give about envying sinners and fearing the LORD?
options: Do not envy sinners; fear the LORD all day long
Envy sinners to learn from them; fear the LORD occasionally
Ignore sinners and forget the LORD
Envy sinners but also fear the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Do not envy sinners; fear the LORD all day long
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:17 instructs, 'Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long,' promoting consistent reverence over envy.

questions.question: What assurance does Proverbs 23:18 give about the future for those who live wisely?
options: There is an end and expectation will not be cut off
questions.correctAnswer: There is an end and expectation will not be cut off
questions.explanation: Verse 18 says, 'For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off,' promising hope and fulfillment for the wise.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:19 encourage the son to do?
options: Be wise and guide thine heart in the way
questions.correctAnswer: Be wise and guide thine heart in the way
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way,' emphasizing personal responsibility in wisdom.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:20, which group of people should one avoid associating with?
options: Winebibbers and riotous eaters of flesh
questions.correctAnswer: Winebibbers and riotous eaters of flesh
questions.explanation: Verse 20 warns, 'Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh,' advising to avoid those who indulge excessively in drunkenness and gluttony.

questions.question: What consequence does Proverbs 23:21 associate with drunkenness and gluttony?
options: They shall come to poverty and be clothed with rags
They will be respected in society
questions.correctAnswer: They shall come to poverty and be clothed with rags
questions.explanation: Verse 21 states, 'For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags,' linking indulgence with ruin.

questions.question: What instruction does Proverbs 23:22 give about one's parents?
options: Hearken unto thy father and despise not thy mother when she is old
Despise your parents if they grow old
questions.correctAnswer: Hearken unto thy father and despise not thy mother when she is old
questions.explanation: The verse teaches respect for both father and mother, especially in their old age.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:23 advise believers to 'buy' and never 'sell'?
questions.explanation: Verse 23 says, 'Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding,' encouraging valuing spiritual treasures over material wealth.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:24, how does the father of a righteous child feel?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice,' showing the joy brought by a wise child.

questions.question: What promise is given in Proverbs 23:25 about the feelings of parents toward a wise child?
options: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice
questions.correctAnswer: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice
questions.explanation: Verse 25 explicitly says, 'Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice,' emphasizing parental joy from a wise offspring.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:26 urge a son to give to his father?
options: His heart and to observe his ways
questions.correctAnswer: His heart and to observe his ways
questions.explanation: Verse 26 says, 'My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways,' encouraging wholehearted obedience and attentiveness.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 23:17 encourages believers to envy sinners as a way to learn from them.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:17 states, 'Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long,' clearly advising against envying sinners.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 23 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 23.

questions.question: What should one consider diligently when eating with a ruler?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee' (Proverbs 23:1). This indicates that one should be mindful of the food they are about to consume.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23, what happens to riches?
questions.explanation: The text says, 'for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven' (Proverbs 23:5), suggesting transient nature of wealth.

questions.question: What should one do if tempted by the bread of someone with an evil eye?
questions.explanation: The verse advises, 'Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats' (Proverbs 23:6), indicating to avoid food from those who are deceitful.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:13 suggest about correcting a child?
questions.explanation: The instruction is clear: 'Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die' (Proverbs 23:13). This emphasizes the importance of discipline.

questions.question: What is the fate of the drunkard and the glutton according to Proverbs 23?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty' (Proverbs 23:21), warning against excess and indulgence.

questions.question: Which command is given regarding one's parents in Proverbs 23?
questions.explanation: The verse instructs, 'Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old' (Proverbs 23:22), highlighting the importance of respecting parents.

questions.question: What is the relationship between a wise child and their father according to Proverbs 23:24?
questions.explanation: The text states, 'The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise child shall have joy of him' (Proverbs 23:24), connecting wisdom with parental joy.

questions.question: What is a key warning given about wine in Proverbs 23?
options: Look not upon it when it is red
questions.correctAnswer: Look not upon it when it is red
questions.explanation: The verse warns, 'Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright' (Proverbs 23:31), advising against temptation.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:27 compare a whore to?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit' (Proverbs 23:27), using metaphor to describe the dangers of promiscuity.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:29, who experiences woe and sorrow?
questions.explanation: The verse questions, 'Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?' (Proverbs 23:29), implying these are traits of the drunkard.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 23 advises to seek truth and wisdom and not to sell it.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding' (Proverbs 23:23), affirming the value of these virtues.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 23:18 states that the expectation of the righteous shall be cut off.
questions.explanation: The verse asserts, 'For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off' (Proverbs 23:18), indicating that expectations for the righteous will not be lost.

questions.question: Which New Testament teaching echoes the warning against drunkenness found in Proverbs 23?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:18 states, 'And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit,' which resonates with the warnings about wine in Proverbs 23.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Proverbs 23 when contrasting the wise with the foolish?
questions.explanation: The chapter employs parallelism, a common Hebrew literary device, to juxtapose contrasting ideas such as wisdom and folly throughout its verses.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word for 'heart' (לב, lev) imply in Proverbs 23:26 about one's focus?
questions.explanation: The term 'heart' in Hebrew (לב, lev) signifies not just emotion but the inner self and will, as indicated in Proverbs 23:26, urging one to give their heart and observe ways.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 23 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 23 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:4 teach about the pursuit of wealth?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:4 explicitly states, 'Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom,' warning against the futility of seeking wealth.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:12, what should one apply their heart and ears to?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:12 instructs to 'Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge', emphasizing the importance of gaining wisdom.

questions.question: What warning does Proverbs 23:20 provide regarding social behaviors?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:20 warns 'Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh,' indicating the dangers of associating with those who indulge excessively.

questions.question: Proverbs 23:25 describes the joy of which family members when a wise child is raised?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:25 states, 'Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice,' highlighting parental joy in a wise child.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:7 imply about the nature of a person's thoughts?
options: They can be hidden from others
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:7 states, 'For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he,' indicating that one's inner thoughts directly correlate with their outward behavior.

questions.question: In Proverbs 23:14, what is the result of correcting a child?
options: It shall deliver his soul from hell
questions.correctAnswer: It shall deliver his soul from hell
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:14 asserts, 'Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell', emphasizing the spiritual significance of proper correction.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:30 indicate about those who seek wine?
options: They that tarry long at the wine
questions.correctAnswer: They that tarry long at the wine
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:30 notes, 'They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine,' warning of the dangers associated with excessive drinking.

questions.question: What theological principle can be drawn from Proverbs 23:18 regarding hope?
options: There is an end and expectation shall not be cut off
questions.correctAnswer: There is an end and expectation shall not be cut off
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:18 teaches that 'For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off,' affirming the hopeful nature of faith in God's promises.

questions.question: In Proverbs 23:11, who is said to be mighty and will plead the cause of the fatherless?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:11 states, 'For their redeemer is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee,' indicating God's protective role over the vulnerable.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:28 warn about the strange woman?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:27 warns, 'For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit,' illustrating the dangers of sexual immorality.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 23:5 describe the nature of wealth?
options: It is a source of happiness
It is a gift from God
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:5 states, 'for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven,' illustrating the transient nature of wealth.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 23:9 say about speaking to a fool?
options: He will despise the wisdom of thy words
questions.correctAnswer: He will despise the wisdom of thy words
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:9 warns, 'Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words,' indicating the futility of sharing wisdom with those who reject it.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Proverbs 23:17 concerning sinners?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:17 states, 'Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long,' emphasizing God's justice in the judgment of sinners.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Proverbs 23:6 and 23:8 convey about accepting gifts?
options: They can be deceitful and harmful
questions.correctAnswer: They can be deceitful and harmful
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:6 warns against eating the bread of a man with an evil eye, while Proverbs 23:8 states that the morsel eaten shall be vomited up, highlighting the potential harm in accepting deceitful gifts.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 23:22, what is the duty concerning one's parents?
options: Listen to your father and mother
questions.correctAnswer: Listen to your father and mother
questions.explanation: Proverbs 23:22 states, 'Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old,' emphasizing the importance of honoring and listening to one's parents.
